In summary, our research is concerned with
the influence of substrate modification, polypeptide truncations and axial ligand on the active site molecular structure of HO.
the molecular structure of the heme oxygenase active site in the resting and catalytic states, and how it is influenced by the substrate and the axial ligands.

how the active site structure of heme oxygenase is modulated by substrate, axial ligand and protein environment, and how this influences the molecular and electronic structure of the substrate, and the subsequent product distribution.

the electronic structure of PH, and its seating in hHO, is largely independent of the polypeptide length, substrate modification or axial ligand.

The main takeaway from our work is that
, while the electronic structure of the active site is largely conserved, the molecular structure, and hence the steric environment, is not.

the substrate seating of heme in HO is not a rigidly defined structure, but is subject to significant environmental influences, which are likely to have a profound influence on the catalytic mechanism of HO.
